title: Usage Attribution Hands-on Workshop
next_steps: Set up trial tenant with route-level telemetry by 2026-01-18
Run 2-week pilot capturing per-route token breakdowns; Redwood to provide sample prompts and cost baseline
Send SOC2 + security pack and onboarding checklist
action_items: Alicia Park: provision trial tenant, invite Cobalt Health team (due 2026-01-18)
Miguel Santos: create benchmark script for Cobalt's typical chat workload (due 2026-01-20)
Priya Nair: provide representative prompt corpus and traffic patterns (due 2026-01-19)
Lena Zhou: confirm internal chargeback code mappings and routing tags (due 2026-01-22)
summary: Hands-on workshop to show Redwood Console's per-route usage analytics, cost slicing, and Optimize suggestions. Covered tagging, cohort comparisons, batch/cache levers, hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, and pilot plan.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-01-15 | Time: 16:00 PST | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Redwood (Alicia, Miguel, Diane) + Cobalt Health (Priya, Tom, Lena, Rahul)
transcript:
00:00 Alicia Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you squeezing this in, uh we'll do a hands-on run through the console and then walk through the pilot plan
00:18 Priya Nair: great thanks Alicia, excited — we want to see how to attribute costs back to product teams, and how to spot regressions quickly
00:34 Miguel Santos: forgive me if I jump in with the demo steps; I'll share my screen. we built a route-level telemetry model so each API route maps to a product tag, so you can break down per-route token cost
01:12 Tom Baxter: quick Q, are routes the same as endpoints or can we do path + tag? like, our infra uses route groups
01:26 Miguel Santos: good question. you can do endpoint, path, or any tag keys — we support multi-key routing. so you can slice by service, by business unit, by prompt template
02:03 Lena Zhou: can we show the cost allocation? our finops team needs CSVs for chargeback
02:15 Alicia Park: yep, exportable reports, and you can automate daily dumps to S3; also the console has a chargeback view that maps to cost centers
03:05 Miguel Santos: ok sharing screen now... landing page, usage lenses, and here's the per-route overview. notice the small spike at 10:22 yesterday — that's the cohort filter at work
03:28 Rahul Mehra: sorry mic was muted, can you zoom into the batching suggestions section? that's the part we care about for latency vs cost
03:42 Miguel Santos: sure. under Optimize we show workload-aware batching recs: recommended batch size, estimated token savings, and latency impact. these are derived from your sequence length distribution
04:10 Priya Nair: are those recommendations model-specific? we run multiple open models and some hosted variants
04:22 Miguel Santos: yes model-specific and hardware aware — we profile on the model catalog and show per-model kernel/quantization suggestions. the recs include an estimated % cost reduction and a confidence score
05:00 Tom Baxter: on private deployments — if we want to run this in our VPC, does the console still give the same telemetry?
05:12 Alicia Park: console is a control plane option; in private mode we can ship a data plane collector that forwards anonymized telemetry to your compliance bucket, and you keep keys — KMS and audit logs intact
05:45 Lena Zhou: encryption at rest and in transit, and SOC 2 docs? we need that before legal signs off
05:53 Alicia Park: we'll attach the SOC2 pack, ISO cert summary, and SSO/SAML integration guide in the follow-up pack
06:30 Miguel Santos: jumping back to the dashboard — here's per-route token breakdown: prompt tokens, completion tokens, and system tokens. you can group by day, by release tag, or by model variant
07:05 Miguel Santos: note: automatic prefix caching is shown as a separate savings line — if you have repeated system prompts or few-shot examples we estimate KV cache hit rate and cost avoidance
07:52 Priya Nair: that KV cache number looks optimistic — how do you calculate hit rate?
08:05 Miguel Santos: we use sequence similarity heuristics plus route-level locality. it's an estimate, we recommend running the pilot to validate for your traffic
09:00 Tom Baxter: are we able to annotate requests with our internal ticket IDs so the console picks that up for chargeback?
09:14 Miguel Santos: yes — any metadata you send as headers can be surfaced and used as grouping keys, you just map them as route tags
10:02 Alicia Park: demo note: we clicked into a route called /triage-chat — you can see distribution of latencies, P95, P99, and the inferred cost per thousand calls. comparing model variants M1-quant vs M1-fp16 shows a 37% cost delta
11:00 Lena Zhou: nice — can the RBAC restrict who sees cost vs who sees usage only?
11:12 Diane Ho: yes role-based views are configurable; we typically set FinOps to cost-read, ML to model-exec, and devs to debug-only views
12:05 Priya Nair: talk me through a real example — say a weekly spike, how do we trace root cause?
12:18 Miguel Santos: jump to the timeline, enable correlated logs, and then pivot to prompt sample view — we show representative prompts alongside token counts so you can spot a prompt drift that inflates tokens
13:05 Tom Baxter: is there an API for pulling the per-route metrics? we want to feed it into our internal BI
13:15 Miguel Santos: yep REST endpoints and SDKs, streaming webhooks for near-realtime; we'll share sample code in the repo link
14:00 Rahul Mehra: about performance testing — can Redwood run a benchmark that mimics our 90th percentile production pattern?
14:12 Miguel Santos: absolutely. that's part of the pilot. I'll prepare a workload script that replays your sequence length distribution and concurrency profile against hosted and dedicated configs
15:05 Priya Nair: on success criteria, we want to see a 20% reduction in token spend or improved P95 latency under same cost — is that reasonable?
15:20 Alicia Park: totally reasonable, and we'll baseline current spend then run Optimize recs (batching, cache, model swap) and report delta
16:02 Lena Zhou: any gotchas with quantized models? we've seen hallucination spikes when moving to int8 in other infra
16:20 Miguel Santos: good point — quantization can affect output quality. Redwood Optimize surfaces quality regressions by running your eval prompt set; you'll want to flag critical evals so we can gate rollouts
17:10 Tom Baxter: can we set automatic fallback to a safer model if quality regressions are detected?
17:22 Miguel Santos: yes — rollout policies support canary thresholds and automatic fallback to pinned model version if eval metrics exceed thresholds
18:05 Priya Nair: regarding costs for Dedicated vs Hosted — how do we compute the unit economics? we have steady baseline and some spiky periods
18:22 Alicia Park: we show a break-even analysis in the console: estimated monthly cost for hosted versus committed instance costs for Dedicated, factoring burst buffers and preemptible savings
19:00 Miguel Santos: also show the routing policy — you can route low-latency traffic to Dedicated and burst to Hosted when Dedicated saturates; cost modelling includes both
20:12 Lena Zhou: can the UI tag noisy routes so we can throttle or set budgets?
20:25 Miguel Santos: yes budget alerts and auto-throttling per route; an option to apply per-route quotas or cost caps
21:05 Rahul Mehra: curious about data residency — if we run in EU region can logs and telemetry be kept within region?
21:18 Alicia Park: yes region pinning and VPC peering; private flow keeps data in-region, audit logs are exportable to your SIEM
22:05 Priya Nair: show us the cohort compare feature — we want to compare pre/post model swap for a subset of users
22:18 Miguel Santos: here's cohort compare: pick date range, pick route, pick cohort tag (we used "beta-users"), and you get side-by-side token distribution and quality eval diff
23:05 Tom Baxter: there was a mention of cost per inference — can that be normalized per 1k calls across differing models?
23:20 Miguel Santos: yes we normalize to cost per 1k calls and show relative and absolute numbers; you can also normalize by token or by response size
24:00 Alicia Park: small aside — for procurement we offer Reserved Capacity commits for Dedicated with monthly true-ups and burst pools
24:35 Priya Nair: legal will ask about data retention default, can we set retention shorter?
24:44 Alicia Park: retention policies configurable per account; private deployments can adhere to your org defaults
25:30 Miguel Santos: pivoting to the notebooks integration — we can surface per-route insights into your infra notebooks so SREs can run root cause analyses inline
26:05 Priya Nair: ok can you demo the CSV export for chargeback?
26:12 Miguel Santos: exporting now... choose grouping keys, choose date range, choose columns. exported file includes token breakdown, model, route tags, and cost attribution columns
27:05 Lena Zhou: perfect. can the export include our internal cost center code column?
27:22 Miguel Santos: if you send that header we map it; otherwise you can attach a lookup CSV and we join on route tags
28:10 Tom Baxter: anything we should worry about for rollout? specifically do you recommend a small canary or a wide rollout?
28:22 Miguel Santos: start small: pick low-risk routes, run the eval set, enable automatic rollback; we can also run a canary that mirrors traffic to staging
29:05 Priya Nair: what's the plan for the 2-week pilot?
29:12 Alicia Park: 1) baseline week — collect telemetry, 2) apply Optimize recs and run bench, 3) compare metrics and quality, 4) present final report. we'll have weekly check-ins and an end-of-pilot review
30:00 Rahul Mehra: are there charges for the pilot?
30:10 Alicia Park: pilot baseline is free for telemetry collection; if you want Redwood-managed benchmark runs on Dedicated there may be a small engineering fee; we'll outline in the next steps
31:05 Tom Baxter: any references or docs we can read while we wait?
31:12 Diane Ho: we'll send the console quickstart, Optimize whitepaper, and sample benchmarking scripts link
32:00 Priya Nair: quick question — how do you handle prompt versions? we have multiple prompt revisions in prod and want versioned attribution
32:15 Miguel Santos: we support prompt versioning via tags; you can pin a prompt hash and see per-prompt token usage over time
33:00 Lena Zhou: can you show us the alerting UI for cost anomalies?
33:12 Miguel Santos: sure. anomaly alerts let you set thresholds or use statistical detection; you can route alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or email and include a diagnostics snapshot
34:00 Alicia Park: closing couple minutes, recap: Redwood to provision trial tenant, Miguel to run bench script, Cobalt to share prompts and mapping, Redwood to send SOC2 + pilot plan
34:25 Priya Nair: thanks all — excited to run the pilot, main goal is clear chargeback and 20% cost reduction target
34:40 Miguel Santos: great; I'll follow up with the GitHub link and the workload artifact
35:05 Tom Baxter: one last nit — can we set up a dummy route so finance can test the CSV ingest?
35:15 Alicia Park: yes we'll create a test route in the tenant for you to push sample traffic
35:30 Rahul Mehra: thanks everyone, talk soon
35:38 Alicia Park: thanks, we'll send notes and next steps; bye
35:45 [call ends]

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-heard product names (we recorded M1-quant as M1-quantized sometimes), filler words, and some overlap. Links shared: https://redwood.ai/console-quickstart, https://redwood.ai/optimize-whitepaper, repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pilot-scripts
duration_alignment_note: Transcript spans ~35 minutes of speaking and Q&A; meeting software auto-trimmed some silence; total calendar duration 58m (includes pre/post discussions).
